item.description:
STORY | Punjab farm fires spike: 672 of 1,007 cases from three districts

The number of farm fire incidents in Punjab has nearly doubled in the past week, with a single-day increase of 194 cases, bringing the cumulative total to 1,007.

Of these incidents, 672 were reported from three districts: Tarn Taran, Amritsar, and Ferozepur.

According to official data, Punjab recorded 542 farm fire incidents between September 15 and October 23 this year.

As of October 28, the total number of incidents was 813, and with the recent spike of 194 on October 29, the total has now reached 1,007, the data showed.

Of the 1,007 farm fire incidents, Tarn Taran accounted for a major chunk of these at 397 cases, followed by Amritsar at 171 and Ferozepur at 104.

The data showed that over 90 per cent of the total area of paddy cultivated in Tarn Taran and Amritsar has already been harvested.

So far, fines totalling over Rs 17 lakh have been imposed as environmental compensation in 349 cases of stubble burning, with over Rs 13 lakh already recovered.

item.title: 🌐 🚨 UPDATE: POLYMARKET WALLET-DRAIN INCIDENT TRACED TO MALICIOUS CODE IN A DEBUGBEAR MONITORING SCRIPT In an Oct 29 analysis, Hudson Rock says a...
item.description:
🌐 🚨 UPDATE: POLYMARKET WALLET-DRAIN INCIDENT TRACED TO MALICIOUS CODE IN A DEBUGBEAR MONITORING SCRIPT

In an Oct 29 analysis, Hudson Rock says a DebugBear-hosted performance-monitoring script loaded by Polymarket contained wallet-draining code aimed at logged-in trading sessions. Polymarket's status page says "one of our third party providers was compromised"; it halted trading and marked the incident resolved at 3:05 PM ET.

• The script searched the page for the user's live trading client and signer, then tried to sell positions or move tokens and balances to an attacker-set address
• It read stored auth context, including CLOB API key data, and reported wallet and portfolio details back to its operator
• Polymarket's production build records removal of the DebugBear script (build time 1:59 PM ET)
• Polymarket says anyone impacted will be made whole and it has referred the case to law enforcement

⚠️ Analyst Note:
Polymarket's notice does not name the supplier; the DebugBear link rests on Hudson Rock's script capture and Polymarket's build metadata. Victim count and total losses are NOT confirmed, and attempted transactions are not proof of completed theft. Nothing shows other DebugBear customers were hit. Review recent orders and wallet activity from a clean session and reject unexpected signing requests.

item.title: 🚨 UPDATE: PALO ALTO CONFIRMS PHP2SHELL EXPLOITATION OF EXPOSED PAN-OS MANAGEMENT INTERFACES Palo Alto Networks says PHP2Shell (CVE-2026-109618 / CV...
item.description:
🚨 UPDATE: PALO ALTO CONFIRMS PHP2SHELL EXPLOITATION OF EXPOSED PAN-OS MANAGEMENT INTERFACES

Palo Alto Networks says PHP2Shell (CVE-2026-109618 / CVE-2026-109619) is being actively exploited against PAN-OS management interfaces exposed to the internet. In its Oct 29 update, Unit 42 says it independently verified the attacker tooling and results reported by Dream Research.

• The attackers chained PHP2Shell with the "Fragnesia" Linux kernel privilege escalation (CVE-2026-46300) to get root on the devices
• Dream's recovered artifacts point to 25 rooted PAN-OS firewall/management servers (servers, not organizations) in the US, Japan, Taiwan and South Korea
• Palo Alto says about 0.02% of its installed base had internet-facing management interfaces and was impacted; those customers were contacted individually
• PAN-OS hotfixes are now out across the 10.2–12.2 branches (11.1.7-h12 was the latest released); patched devices are not affected

⚠️ Analyst Note:
This is separate from Unit 42's retracted Oct 23 claim about a European government intrusion. The 25 figure is Dream's artifact-based finding, not a Palo Alto count. Remove public access to management interfaces, restrict them to trusted internal IPs, apply the fix for your exact branch from the advisory's version matrix, and check exposed devices for signs of compromise.

https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/cve-2026-109618-cve-2026-109619/
#DDW #PHP2Shell #PaloAlto #PANOS #CyberSecurity
